With 64 shared uniform draws, duplicate negatives repeat denominator terms in sampled cross-entropy and negative penalties in gBCE; deduplicating changes their weights and sampling probabilities. Mask the current target per position in both losses. Ordinary candidate-set CE is not automatically corrected sampled softmax: correction subtracts log expected sample counts, using multiplicities for replacement sampling or inclusion probabilities for unique sampling. Uniform corrections cancel only when identical across all candidate logits; a separately inserted positive can require different treatment. Apply temperature as score/τ before correction. [TensorFlow sampling](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/random/uniform_candidate_sampler), [sampled softmax](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/nn/sampled_softmax_loss).

gBCE uses L=[−β log σ(s+)−Σ log σ(−s−)]/(m+1), β=1−t+tα, α=k/(|I|−1) under the paper’s uniform-negative setup. t=0 gives BCE; t=1 targets calibration under its assumptions. Calibration t is not temperature. Neither loss automatically removes historical positives. With masking, distinguish 64 proposed draws from m valid negatives: specify duplicate handling, refill versus discard, and reduction. Per-row division by m+1 differs from global averaging or separately averaging positive/negative terms. Calibration depends on actual expected negative exposure and eligible support; substituting realized m for k does not generally restore the theorem after history-dependent filtering. Define zero-negative handling explicitly. [gSASRec paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192), [implementation](https://github.com/asash/gsasrec).

Sampling-policy implication: excluding every known training positive avoids penalizing later interactions, but uses future-within-training information at earlier prediction positions and changes the learning objective. Prefix-only exclusion preserves temporal availability but can label later positives as negatives. Neither establishes preference for unobserved items. Compare policies through macro validation HR@10; calibration improvements alone do not establish ranking gains.
